Amram et al.</td><td>2025</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="amram-2024fjg-detail" data-tags="open data|foundation models"><td colspan="3">

Aspen Open Jets, about 178 M jets from CMS 2016 open data, for pre-training foundation models.

Derives about 178 M high-$p_T$ jets from CMS 2016 open data and pre-trains the OmniJet-α foundation model on them. Pre-training on collision data improves the generation of the simulated top and QCD jets of JetClass despite the domain shift.

<tr class="row" id="elitez-2025aqs" data-tags="reconstruction"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="elitez-2025aqs-detail">ColliderML: The First Release of an OpenDataDetector High-Luminosity Physics Benchmark Dataset</button></td><td>D. Elitez et al.</td><td>2025</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="elitez-2025aqs-detail" data-tags="reconstruction"><td colspan="3">

ColliderML, one million fully simulated HL-LHC events in the OpenDataDetector, for detector-level machine learning.

Experiment-agnostic collisions at 14 TeV with a mean pile-up of 200, across ten Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model processes plus single-particle samples, fully simulated, digitised and reconstructed, and published on Hugging Face.

<tr class="row" id="govorkova-2021hqu" data-tags="anomaly detection|real-time inference"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="govorkova-2021hqu-detail">LHC physics dataset for unsupervised New Physics detection at 40 MHz</button></td><td>E. Govorkova et al.</td><td>2022</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="govorkova-2021hqu-detail" data-tags="anomaly detection|real-time inference"><td colspan="3">

A simulated trigger-level event stream for unsupervised new-physics detection at 40 MHz.

Emulates the data stream of a real-time event-selection system, pre-filtered by requiring an electron or muon, so that new selection strategies and their sensitivity to new phenomena can be developed under trigger constraints.

PILArNet, open 2D and 3D simulated data for liquid-argon time projection chambers.

Described by its authors as the first open 2D and 3D dataset for liquid-argon time projection chambers, with 300,000 samples in three volume sizes for key reconstruction tasks.

<tr class="row" id="komiske-2019jim" data-tags="open data|jet tagging"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="komiske-2019jim-detail">Exploring the Space of Jets with CMS Open Data</button></td><td>P. T. Komiske et al.</td><td>2020</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="komiske-2019jim-detail" data-tags="open data|jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

Jets from CMS 2011 open data, and the metric space of jets measured with the energy mover's distance.

Isolates 1,690,984 central jets with transverse momentum above 375 GeV from 2.3 fb⁻¹ of 7 TeV CMS open data and compares them with simulation. The energy mover's distance between jets is used to study the space of jets and the effect of the detector.

<tr class="row" id="krause-2024avx" data-tags="fast simulation|generative models"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="krause-2024avx-detail">CaloChallenge 2022: a community challenge for fast calorimeter simulation</button></td><td>C. Krause et al.</td><td>2025</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="krause-2024avx-detail" data-tags="fast simulation|generative models"><td colspan="3">

The Fast Calorimeter Simulation Challenge 2022, 31 generative models compared on four shower datasets.

Compares variational autoencoders, GANs, normalizing flows, diffusion and flow-matching models on showers from a few hundred to tens of thousands of voxels, by shower quality, generation time and model size. Quality is measured with histograms, KPD and FPD scores, classifier AUCs and a multiclass classifier.

<tr class="row-detail" id="atlas-2024rua-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

Performance and systematic uncertainties of machine-learning top taggers in full ATLAS simulation.

Evaluates several machine-learning top taggers on simulated 13 TeV ATLAS events and estimates their systematic uncertainties with an approximate procedure. The dataset, with its systematic variations, is public.

<tr class="row-detail" id="benato-2024lnj-detail" data-tags="inference"><td colspan="3">

The FAIR Universe HiggsML Uncertainty challenge, confidence intervals from imperfect simulators.

Participants reported confidence intervals for a parameter of interest of the Higgs boson while accounting for systematic uncertainties, on a tabular dataset of 280 million simulated collisions with 28 features.

Bukhari et al.</td><td>2024</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="bukhari-2023ezc-detail" data-tags="neutrino physics|reconstruction"><td colspan="3">

The three winning solutions of the IceCube Kaggle competition.

Describes the data handling, architecture and training of each and compares them on the Kaggle dataset. The best reaches an angular resolution better than 5° for cascades above 10 TeV and better than 0.5° for tracks, comparable to the state of the art.

<tr class="row-detail" id="amrouche-2021nbs-detail" data-tags="reconstruction"><td colspan="3">

The TrackML throughput phase, which scored the speed of track finding together with its accuracy.

Run on Codalab, where submitted software was executed in a controlled environment. The best three solutions combined good accuracy with an order of magnitude more speed than the state of the art when the challenge was designed.

Aarrestad et al.</td><td>2022</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="aarrestad-2021oeb-detail" data-tags="anomaly detection"><td colspan="3">

The Dark Machines challenge, a billion-event benchmark for unsupervised new-physics searches.

Proposes anomaly scores to define model-independent signal regions, releases more than a billion simulated 13 TeV events equivalent to 10 fb⁻¹, and compares anomaly-detection and density-estimation algorithms in realistic analysis settings.

<tr class="row-detail" id="kasieczka-2021xcg-detail" data-tags="anomaly detection"><td colspan="3">

The LHC Olympics 2020, a community challenge for anomaly detection, with its datasets and results.

Participants developed methods on an R&D dataset and applied them to black boxes holding an unknown anomaly, or none. The paper reviews the unsupervised, weakly supervised and semi-supervised methods submitted and their results.

<tr class="row-detail" id="amrouche-2019wmx-detail" data-tags="reconstruction"><td colspan="3">

The TrackML accuracy phase on Kaggle in 2018, track finding at HL-LHC pile-up.

Participants connected about 100,000 points per event into some 10,000 particle trajectories. The paper shows that the competition's single score selects the best algorithms from the point of view of the domain.

Pata et al.</td><td>2024</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="pata-2023rhh-detail" data-tags="reconstruction"><td colspan="3">

Scalable graph and transformer models for particle flow in full simulation of e⁺e⁻ collisions.

Compares a graph neural network with a kernel-based transformer on tracks and calorimeter clusters. The best model improves the jet transverse momentum resolution by up to 50% over the rule-based algorithm.

<tr class="row-detail" id="shlomi-2020ufi-detail" data-tags="reconstruction|jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

A set-to-graph network that finds secondary vertices inside jets.

<tr class="row-detail" id="bogatskiy-2020tje-detail" data-tags="jet tagging|equivariance"><td colspan="3">

A neural network fully equivariant under the Lorentz group.

Built on finite-dimensional representations of the Lorentz group with tensor-product nonlinearities, it gives simpler, more interpretable models with competitive top-tagging performance.

<tr class="row-detail" id="nachman-2020lpy-detail" data-tags="anomaly detection"><td colspan="3">

ANODE, anomaly detection with neural density estimates in the signal region and sidebands.

Interpolates the sideband density into the signal region to form a likelihood ratio of data to background, which also estimates the background directly.

<tr class="row-detail" id="qu-2019gqs-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

ParticleNet, a dynamic graph convolutional network on jets as particle clouds.

Represents a jet as an unordered set of its particles, which respects their permutation symmetry, and improves markedly on earlier methods on two tagging benchmarks.

<tr class="row-detail" id="butter-2019cae-detail" data-tags="event generation|generative models"><td colspan="3">

A generative adversarial network for LHC events, shown on top-pair production.

Avoids inefficient unweighting and describes intermediate on-shell particles, phase-space boundaries and tails, helped by a maximum mean discrepancy term.

<tr class="row" id="hermans-2019ioj" data-tags="inference"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="hermans-2019ioj-detail">Likelihood-free MCMC with Amortized Approximate Ratio Estimators</button></td><td>J. Hermans et al.</td><td>2019</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="hermans-2019ioj-detail" data-tags="inference"><td colspan="3">

Amortised estimators of the likelihood-to-evidence ratio, used inside MCMC.

One trained ratio estimator gives the likelihood ratios between states of a Markov chain, so the posterior can be sampled without the likelihood.

<tr class="row" id="komiske-2018cqr" data-tags="jet tagging"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="komiske-2018cqr-detail">Energy Flow Networks: Deep Sets for Particle Jets</button></td><td>P. T. Komiske et al.</td><td>2019</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="komiske-2018cqr-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

Energy and Particle Flow Networks, permutation-invariant networks for jets built on Deep Sets.

Energy Flow Networks are infrared and collinear safe by construction; Particle Flow Networks admit general energy dependence and particle information such as charge and flavour. The quark and gluon jets used in the paper are public.

<p class="row-tags"><button type="button" class="tag" data-tag="jet tagging">jet tagging</button></p>

<tr class="row" id="louppe-2017ipp" data-tags="jet tagging"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="louppe-2017ipp-detail">QCD-Aware Recursive Neural Networks for Jet Physics</button></td><td>G. Louppe et al.</td><td>2019</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="louppe-2017ipp-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

Recursive neural networks that follow a jet's clustering history.

Treats four-momenta as words and the sequential-recombination clustering tree as the parse of a sentence; the recursive networks are more accurate and data efficient than image-based ones.

<p class="row-tags"><button type="button" class="tag" data-tag="jet tagging">jet tagging</button></p>

<tr class="row-detail" id="paganini-2017dwg-detail" data-tags="fast simulation|generative models"><td colspan="3">

CaloGAN, generative adversarial networks for showers in a multilayer electromagnetic calorimeter.

Achieves speed-ups of 100 to 1000 over full simulation on CPU and up to about 10⁵ on GPU, and reproduces geometric shower-shape properties of photons, positrons and charged pions.

<tr class="row" id="baldi-2016fzo" data-tags="event classification"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="baldi-2016fzo-detail">Parameterized neural networks for high-energy physics</button></td><td>P. Baldi et al.</td><td>2016</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="baldi-2016fzo-detail" data-tags="event classification"><td colspan="3">

Parameterized neural networks, which take physics parameters such as a particle's mass as input.

One network interpolates smoothly between parameter values and replaces a set of classifiers trained at individual values, with improved performance at intermediate values.
